Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Oold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagrnahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SEQETARY 05 January 2007 DIRECTOR QUIRINO M. UBUNAO DILG Regional Office No. IO Cagayan de Oro City Dear Director Libunao: This pertains to your letter seeking this level's advice/opinion relative to the legal effects and implications vis-å-vis the implementation of the penalty of suspension imposed by the Office of the Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon against Mayor Jose M. Galario, Jr. of Valencia City. You stated that in an Order dated 15 April 2005, then Ombudsman Simeon V. Marcelo found Mayor Galario administratively guilty as charged and thereby imposed upon him the penalty of suspension for three (3) months without pay. Mayor Galario then filed a Motion for Reconsideration and on 13 March 2006, an Order was issued by the Office of the Ombudsman denying the same. Complainant then filed before the Ombudsman a Motion for Execution of Judgment. Accordingly, on 12 October 2006, Ombudsman Merceditas M. Gutierrez issued an Order directing you to immediately implement the Order of the Ombudsman suspending Mayor Galario for three months without pay. On 23 October 2006, Atty. Rodolfo M. Elman, OIC, Office of the Deputy Ombudsman for Mindanao, indorsed to you the Ombudsman Order for immediate implementation. When you were about to implement the same, the Court of Appeals, Special 21 st Division, in a Petition filed by Mayor Galario, entitled: "Jose M. Galario, Jr. vs. The Honorable Office Of the Ombudsman and Ruth P. Piano", docketed as CA-G.R. sp No. 01278-MIN, issued on 23 October 2006 a 60-day Temporary Restraining Order, directing the Ombudsman or any of its agents to refrain from implementing the 11 April 2005 and 13 March 2006 Orders of the Ombudsman. On 28 December 2006, citing that the TRO has already expired, complainant again requested you to implement the same. You then sought clarification from the Ombudsman for Mindanao as to whether or not the suspension order can be reimplemented in view of the expiration Of the TRO and in a letter dated 02 January 2007, Honorable Humprey T. Monteroso, Deputy Ombudsman for Mindanao, wrote you and

-2- opined that there is no reason for the delay of implementing the Ombudsman Order of suspension against Mayor Galario, the reason being that the TRO has already expired and the court did not issue a preliminary injunction, hence, upon the TRO's expiration, the same is deemed automatically vacated per Section 5, Rule 58 of the Rules of Court. On 03 January 2007, you accordingly served the suspension order of Mayor Galario and pursuant to Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code, he likewise required Vice Mayor Benjamin A. Verano to take his oath of office as Acting City Mayor for a period of three (3) months. However, the oath taking did not materialize for the reason that Vice Mayor Verano took a leave Of absence. You then asked the highest ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member, in the person Of SP Member Helen P. Bernal, to now exercise the powers and functions as Acting City Vice Mayor and consequently act as OIC, Office of the Acting City Mayor, for three (3) days in the absence of the Vice Mayor who is on leave; On 04 January 2007, Vice Mayor Verano called and told you that he is no longer taking his oath of office as Acting City Mayor and Will not also vacate the Office of the Vice Mayor. You likewise reported that Mayor Galario wrote you, saying that he will not Step down as he Will avail all legal remedies under the law. Hence, your following queries which we shall quote in toto: I. "Will the 1st ranking Sangguniang Pantungsod Member, Helen P. Bernal fill up the position of the Office of the City Mayor applying the law of succession in view of the refusal of City Vice Mayor Benjamin A. Verano to assume the temporarily vacant Office of the Mayor? 2. Considering that City Vice Mayor Benjamin Verano refuses to assume the position as Acting City Mayor, will the rule on succession still apply from the 1st ranking Sangguniang Pantungsod Member down the line? 3. What are the possible actions that our level could take against City Mayor Galario and City Vice Mayor Verano who up to this writing refuse to vacate their respective positions?" In reply to your ISt and 2nd queries, may we invite your attention to Section 44 (a) of the Local Government Code, which provides that Ifa permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the governor or mayor, the vice governor or vice mayor concerned shall become the goærnor or mayor. If a permanent vacancy occurs in the offices of the governor, vice governor, mayor, or vice mayor, the highest ranking sanggunian member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member shall become the gozærnor, vice governor, mayor or vice mayor, as the case may be.

Subsequent zacancies in the said office shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking as defined herein" On the other hand, Section 46 (a) of the same Code provides that: "When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice governor, city or municipal vice mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions Of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days". It bears to emphasize that Section 44 (a) treats of permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor or in the Offices of the Mayor and Vice Mayor simultaneously. In the latter case, should there be simultaneous vacancies in the Offices of the Mayor and the Vice Mayor, the highest ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member shall become the Mayor and the 2nd highest ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member shall become the Vice Mayor and subsequent vacancies in the Sanggunian shall be filled automatically by the other Sanggunian Members according to their ranking. On the other hand, Section 46 (a) treats of temporary vacancy only in the Office of the Mayor. Parenthetically, said section is silent on the temporary vacancy in the Office of the Vice Mayor. For that matter, even the entire Local Government Code is silent on this regard. However, in the case of Menzon vs. Petilla (197 SCRA 251), the Supreme Court ruled that in case of temporary vacancy in the Office of the Vice Mayor and the Local Government Code is silent, then the rule on permanent vacancy in the Office of the Vice Mayor can be analogously applied, thereby allowing the highest ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member to assume as Acting Vice Mayor, so as not to cause a hiatus in the office. Going now to your queries nos. 1 and 2, it bears to emphasize that under Section 456 of the Local Government Code, it is one of the powers and duties Of the Vice Mayor to, among others, exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the City Mayor in case of temporary vacancy as provided for in Section 46 of the Local Government Code. Relating this to Section 46 (a) of the Code where it is likewise provided that in case of temporary incapacity of the City Mayor to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons, the City Vice Mayor shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Mayor by assuming as Acting Mayor. At this point, it is not amiss to point out that succession to a higher office, whether it be due to a permanent or temporary vacancy, is not only a matter of right but more importantly, it is also a matter of duty of the elective local official concerned mandated by law to succeed. Accordingly, when a temporary vacancy occurs in the Office of the City Mayor, it is not only a right but a duty as well of the City Vice Mayor to

-4- assume as Acting Mayor in order to ensure that the operations of the city, more importantly, the delivery of basic services to the public constituency, shall remain unhampered. A problem will arise if a City Vice Mayor refuses to assume as such. In this regard, it may be instructive to examine the last paragraph of Section 44 of the Local Government Code which enumerated the causes of permanent vacancies, among which is the refusal to assume office by the incumbent. On the other hand, Section 46 of the Local Government Code defined temporary vacancy by way of enumeration, stating that it is the temporary incapacity to perform the duties for physical or legal reasons, such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad and suspension from office. Accordingly, when the Vice Mayor refused to assume as Acting Mayor, such refusal would lead to temporary legal incapacity on his part to assume the functions of his office, thereby rendering also his office deemed temporarily vacant. Seemingly, therefore, with the refusal of the Vice Mayor to assume as Acting Mayor, there will arise a temporary vacancy both in the Offices of the Mayor and the Vice Mayor. It is, however, unfortunate that Section 44 of the Local Government Code treats of permanent vacancies in both offices simultaneously, while Section 46 (a) of the same Code treats of a temporary vacancy only in the Office of the Mayor. The Local Government Code is silent in temporary vacancies occurring both in the Offices of the Mayor and the Vice Mayor. Such vacuum, however, should not prejudice the proper delivery of basic services. Accordingly, as earlier stated in the case of Menzon vs. Petilla, the wisdom of applying the rule on succession in cases of permanent vacancies can be analogously applied in cases of temporary vacancies where the Local Government Code is silent in the latter instance. Hence, there could be legal basis for the ISt and 2nd ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Members to assume office as Acting Mayor and Acting Vice Mayor, respectively. With regard to your 3'd query, the refusal of Mayor Galario to comply with the order of suspension can be brought to the attention of the Office of the Ombudsman for the proper exercise of its power under Section 15 of RA 6770 to impose the punishment of contempt in accordance with the Rules of Court. On the other hand, the unjustifiable refusal of Vice Mayor Verano to assume as Acting Mayor could render him vulnerable to an administrative charge of dereliction of duty. In the meantime, our recognition of the ISt and 2" d ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Members as Acting City Mayor and Acting City Vice Mayor, respectively, is sufficient to allow them to legally discharge the powers, duties and functions of both offices with full recognition from other offices and agencies of the government. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Legal:43/La Very truly yours, RONALD V. PU Secreta M eRlOR Locu SILG07-040013
